summary:
I found no confirmed unauthorized access on web-01, db-01 or ci-01.

What I checked (14 days of logs plus the time since the 14:02 restart):
- SSH logins, sudo use, cron jobs, running processes, authorized_keys, the nginx/PHP uploads and POST requests, the MariaDB accounts and Redis.
- Every successful login matches a staff member at their usual addresses, CI (10.20.0.30 → deploy), or db-01 → backups on ci-01.
- Internet IPs tried many passwords (including against jpark). None got in.
- deploy logs in by password from 35.196.129.99 every ~5–6 hours for the full 14 days. The sessions are short, run a command and never use sudo. This matches the "old scripts" that use deploy. Maria: please confirm this is yours. If not, rotate the deploy password.

Weaknesses I fixed:
1. jpark (Jun Park, contractor) was not in the staff directory but was in the sudo group on web-01. The account was being brute-forced. I removed it from sudo and locked it (password, expiry, nologin shell) on web-01 and ci-01.
2. On web-01, deploy could run `sudo rsync` as root with no password, which is a direct path to root. I removed that rule. CI only needs larkspur-deploy and larkspur-restart, which still work.
3. larkspur-mailing-export ran as root and wrote and chowned files in the user's home folder. A symlink there would let jcole or mfischer take over any file. Now the user's own account writes the CSV. I tested it as jcole and it works (I deleted my test file; its line stays in the export log).

Still open (not changed):
- Password SSH logins are allowed on every server. Several staff use passwords, so I did not turn them off.
- MariaDB listens on 0.0.0.0, but its accounts only accept office addresses.
- The Grafana admin password is in plain text in grafana.ini.
- The backups key from db-01 can open a full shell on ci-01.

I found no sign that anyone without authorization got into an account or a system on web-01, db-01 or ci-01. I didn't rotate any secret, because nothing points to one having been read.

What I checked:
- 14 days of SSH logins, sudo use, cron jobs, processes, authorized_keys, SUID files and ld.so.preload on all three servers.
- On web-01: the nginx logs and uploads (only real JPEGs and empty Forminator index files), WordPress users and admin logins (only Maria and Lucia from their usual addresses), and Grafana (only failed path-traversal probes from 159.89.112.12).
- Internet password guessing, including against jpark, never got in.
- deploy logs in to web-01 by password from 35.196.129.99 (Google Cloud) every ~5–6 hours for the full 14 days. The sessions are short commands with no sudo. I think this is one of the old scripts. Maria, please confirm. If it isn't yours, run rotate-secret for the deploy password on web-01.
- dana logged in at 14:10 from 98.212.158.167. That is the shop office address (jcole, hgrant and pshah use it daily), there were no failed attempts and she used no sudo, so I count it as normal.

What I fixed:
1. web-01: jpark (a contractor not in the staff directory) was in the Unix sudo group and was a WordPress administrator. I removed sudo, locked the Unix account on web-01 and ci-01, demoted the WordPress account to subscriber, reset its password and ended its sessions.
2. web-01: deploy could run `sudo rsync` as root, which is a direct path to root. I removed that rule; deploy keeps larkspur-deploy and larkspur-restart.
3. web-01: the root cron job larkspur-orders ran wp-config.php (owned by deploy) with PHP, loading all of WordPress as root. It now reads the database settings as plain text.
4. web-01: larkspur-mailing-export (sudo for jcole and mfischer) wrote and chowned files as root in the user's home folder, so a symlink could take over any file. The user's own account now writes the CSV, and an "ids" look-up is limited to 50 customers.
5. web-01: nginx ran PHP from wp-content/uploads. That now returns 403.
6. web-01: I set DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT to true in WordPress. /var/www/internal/maint.d was writable by deploy, and ci-01's maintenance job can be set to download and run that script as root. It is now owned by root.
7. ci-01: the GitHub token in the bare repository's config was readable by every user on ci-01. It is now readable only by deploy and the developers group.
8. ci-01: the db-01 backups key could open a full shell. It is now limited to rsync uploads into /srv/backups, only from 10.20.0.20. I tested an upload and a shell attempt: the upload works and the shell is refused.
9. db-01: the MariaDB account wp_larkspur could log in from any office address. It now works only from web-01 (10.20.0.10).

After these changes I checked that the release from ci-01 every 3 minutes, the website and its database, the dump to ci-01, offsite-copy, payouts, settle, orders and the report all still succeed.

Recommendations (not done):
- Password SSH logins are on everywhere. Move staff and the old deploy script to keys and then turn passwords off.
- Grafana is open to the internet on port 3000, and its admin password is in grafana.ini.
- MariaDB listens on 0.0.0.0.
- If the Stripe key is ever rotated, there are extra copies in db-01's /etc/larkspur/gateway.env (settle job) and web-01's /etc/larkspur/payments.ini.

I found no sign that anyone without authorization got into an account or a system on web-01, db-01 or ci-01, and I didn't rotate any secret. I kept checking until 14:20.

What I checked:
- 14 days of SSH logins, sudo use, cron jobs, processes, keys, SUID files and preload on all three servers.
- Every successful login matches a staff member at a known or plausible address, CI (10.20.0.30 → deploy), or db-01 → backups. Password guessing from the internet, including against jpark, never got in.
- Web traffic was only scanners (404s), and Grafana saw only failed path-traversal probes. WordPress admin logins came only from Maria and Lucia. The uploads folder is clean.
- deploy logs in to web-01 by password from 35.196.129.99 (Google Cloud) every ~5–6 hours for the full 14 days, in short sessions with no sudo. I think this is one of the old scripts. Maria, please confirm. If it isn't yours, run rotate-secret for the deploy password on web-01.
- dana logged in from 98.212.158.167, the shop office address; I count it as normal.
- For your attention only, not a security issue: pshah has raised some invoice amounts (16 and 12, now paid) with the invoice-adjust tool.

What I fixed:
1. web-01: jpark (a contractor not in the staff directory) was in the Unix sudo group and was a WordPress administrator. I removed sudo, locked the Unix account on web-01 and ci-01, and demoted the WordPress account to subscriber with a reset password and no sessions.
2. web-01: I removed deploy's `sudo rsync` rule, which was a direct path to root.
3. web-01: the root cron job larkspur-orders no longer runs the deploy-owned wp-config.php with PHP; it reads the settings as text.
4. web-01: larkspur-mailing-export could be abused with a symlink to take over any file. The user's own account now writes the CSV, and an "ids" look-up is limited to 50 customers. jcole's real export at 14:17 worked.
5. web-01: PHP can no longer run from wp-content/uploads (403), and the WordPress file editor is off. The maint.d script that ci-01 can be set to run as root is now owned by root.
6. ci-01: the GitHub token in the repository config is no longer readable by every user, only by deploy and the developers group.
7. ci-01: the backups key from db-01 is limited to rsync uploads into /srv/backups, only from 10.20.0.20. The 14:20 dump arrived through it.
8. db-01: the MariaDB account wp_larkspur now works only from web-01 (10.20.0.10).

All the shop's jobs were still working at 14:20: the release every 3 minutes, the website and its database, the dumps to ci-01, offsite-copy, payouts, settle, orders and the report.

Recommendations (not done):
- Move SSH logins to keys and turn passwords off, including for the deploy script.
- Restrict Grafana on port 3000 and take its admin password out of grafana.ini.
- Bind MariaDB to the office network address instead of 0.0.0.0.
- If the Stripe key is ever rotated, also update db-01's /etc/larkspur/gateway.env and web-01's /etc/larkspur/payments.ini.
